Medina is its place of revelation.

{1} That is: this is a {surah} of great standing, {which We have sent down}, as a mercy from Us to the servants, and We have protected it from every devil. {And We have imposed it}; that is, We have decreed in it what We have decreed of the prescribed punishments (hudud), testimonies and other matters. {And We have sent down in it clear verses}; that is, sublime rulings, commands and prohibitions, and great wisdoms. {So that you may remember}: when We make it clear to you and inform you of what you did not know.

Then he began to explain those rulings referred to, saying:

{2} This ruling concerns the adulterer and the adulteress who are unmarried (al-bikrayn): each of them shall be lashed one hundred lashes. As for the one who is married (al-thayyib), the authentic and well-known Sunnah has established that his punishment is stoning (al-rajm).

God Most High forbade us to let compassion (ra'fah) for them in the religion of God prevent us from carrying out the prescribed punishment upon them, whether it is natural compassion, or on account of kinship, friendship, or anything else. Faith necessitates the removal of this compassion that would prevent the implementation of God's command. Indeed, true mercy lies in carrying out the punishment upon them. Although we may show them mercy because of what has been decreed for them, we do not show them mercy in this respect.

God Most High commanded that a group (ta'ifah), that is, a company of believers, witness the punishment of the two adulterers, so that it may become widely known, so that shame and deterrence may be achieved thereby, and so that they may actually observe the punishment. For witnessing the rulings of the Sharia in practice strengthens knowledge, firmly establishes understanding, and comes closer to hitting the correct judgment, so that nothing is added to it or subtracted from it. And God knows best.

{3} This is an explanation of the vileness of fornication (zina), and that it defiles the honour of its perpetrator and the honour of whoever is joined and mixed with him, in a way that other sins do not. So He informs that the fornicator (zani) does not venture to marry any women except a fornicatress (zaniyah) whose condition suits his condition, or a female polytheist (mushrikah) who does not believe in resurrection or recompense, and does not adhere to the command of God.

Likewise, the fornicatress does not marry anyone except a fornicator or a polytheist. {And that has been forbidden to the believers}; that is, it has been forbidden for them to marry a fornicator or to marry a fornicatress. The meaning of the verse is that whoever is characterised by fornication, whether a man or a woman, and does not repent from it, then the one who ventures to marry him or her, despite God's prohibition of that, is in one of two situations: either he does not adhere to the judgement of God and His Messenger, in which case he is none other than a polytheist; or he adheres to the judgement of God and His Messenger, yet ventures to marry him or her while knowing of their fornication, in which case this marriage is fornication, and the one who marries is a fornicator who commits illicit intercourse (musafih). Had he truly believed in God, he would not have ventured to do that.

This is a clear proof for the prohibition of marrying a fornicatress until she repents, and likewise marrying a fornicator until he repents; for the joining of a husband with his wife and a wife with her husband is the strongest of joinings and pairings. God the Exalted has said: ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their spouses﴾; that is, their companions. So God prohibited that because of the great evil in it, and because it entails little jealousy (ghayrah), the attribution of children who are not of the husband to him, and the fornicator's failure to chastely guard her due to his preoccupation with others; some of which alone is sufficient for the prohibition.

In this is also proof that the fornicator is not a believer, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "A fornicator does not commit fornication while he is a believer." So although he is not a polytheist, the name of praise, which is complete faith (al-iman al-mutlaq), is not applied to him.

**Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 24, verses 4–5:**

{4} When the Exalted magnified the matter of fornication (zina) by making its flogging obligatory, and likewise its stoning if the offender is married (muhsan), and by declaring that it is not permitted to approach it or mix with it in a way that leaves a person safe from evil, He then showed the gravity of assailing people's honour by accusing them of fornication. He said: ﴿And those who accuse chaste women﴾, meaning free women who are chaste, and likewise men; there is no difference between the two. The intended meaning of "accusing" is accusing them of fornication, as indicated by the context. ﴿Then do not produce﴾ in support of what they accused them of ﴿four witnesses﴾, meaning upright men who testify to that explicitly. ﴿Flog them eighty lashes﴾, with a moderate whip that causes pain, and without exaggerating in it to the point of destroying the person, because the purpose is discipline, not destruction.

In this is the establishment of the hadd (the prescribed punishment) for slander (qadhf), but on the condition that the one slandered is, as the Exalted said, chaste and a believer. As for slandering one who is not chaste, it requires ta'zir (discretionary punishment). ﴿And do not accept their testimony ever﴾, meaning this is another penalty for them: the testimony of the slanderer is not accepted, even if he has received the hadd for the slander, until he repents, as will come. ﴿And those are the defiantly disobedient﴾, meaning those who have left the obedience of Allah, whose evil has become great. This is because of violating what Allah has forbidden, violating the honour of his brother, giving people power to speak about him with what he has said, removing the brotherhood that Allah established among the people of faith, and wanting indecency to spread among those who believe. This is evidence that slander is among the major sins.

{5} And His saying: ﴿Except for those who repent after that and reform. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. Repentance in this context means that the slanderer denies his own accusation and acknowledges that he lied in what he said. It is obligatory for him to deny it, even if he is certain that it happened, since he did not bring four witnesses. So when the slanderer repents, reforms his deeds, and replaces his wrongdoing with good, the fisq (defiant disobedience) is removed from him, and likewise his testimony is accepted according to the correct opinion. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, forgiving all sins for whoever repents and turns back to Him.

The slanderer is flogged if he does not bring four witnesses only when he is not a husband. If he is a husband, then it has been mentioned in His saying:

The testimonies of a husband against his wife were made to avert the hadd from him, because it is generally the case that a husband does not accuse his wife, whom whatever defiles her would also defile him, unless he is truthful. Also, he has a right in this matter, and there is concern about attributing to him children who are not his, and other wisdoms that are absent in other cases. So He said:

{6–7} "And those who accuse their wives but have no witnesses except themselves: the testimony of one of them shall be four testimonies by Allah, that he is surely of the truthful." He called it testimony because it takes the place of witnesses, by saying: "I testify by Allah that I am surely of the truthful regarding what I have accused her of." "And the fifth [testimony] is that the curse of Allah be upon him if he is of the liars"; that is, he adds to the fifth testimony, along with the aforementioned testimony, emphasizing those testimonies by invoking the curse upon himself if he is lying. When his li'an (mutual oath-imprecation) is completed, the hadd (prescribed punishment) for slander falls from him.

The apparent meaning of the verses is that this applies even if he names the man with whom he accused her, for his right [to the hadd] falls away along with hers.

Is the hadd imposed on her by the mere li'an of the man and her refusal [to counter-swear], or is she imprisoned? On this, there are two opinions among the scholars. What the evidence indicates is that the hadd is imposed on her, by the proof of His saying: "And it shall avert from her the punishment that she testify four testimonies by Allah that he is surely of the liars," and so on to the end. For if the punishment, which is the hadd, had not become obligatory by his li'an, her li'an would not have averted it.

{8–9} "And it shall avert from her the punishment," that is, the punishment is averted from her if she confronts the husband's testimonies with testimonies of the same kind: "that she testify four testimonies by Allah that he is surely of the liars," and she adds to the fifth, emphasizing that, by invoking the wrath (ghadab) upon herself. When the li'an between them is completed, they are separated [forever], and the child is disowned from the one who made li'an.

The apparent meaning of the verses indicates the requirement of these wordings in the li'an from him and from her, the requirement of their order, that nothing be reduced from them and nothing substituted for another, that li'an is specific to the husband when he accuses his wife and not the reverse, and that resemblance in the child has no weight alongside li'an, just as it is not considered with the marriage bed (firash); resemblance is considered only where nothing else decides.

{10} "And were it not for Allah's grace upon you and His mercy, and that Allah is Oft-Returning, All-Wise." The response to the conditional is omitted, indicated by the context of the discourse; that is: the liar of the two who invoked curses would have been struck by what he invoked upon himself. Among His mercy and grace is the establishment of this particular ruling for the spouses, due to the great need for it, and that He made clear to you the gravity of fornication and the abomination of slandering with it, and that He legislated repentance from these major sins and others.

Since what preceded mentioned the great sin of accusing of fornication in general, this became like an introduction to this story which befell the most noble of women, the Mother of the Believers (may Allah be pleased with her). These verses were revealed concerning the well-known incident of the slander (hadith al-ifk), established in the Sahihs, the Sunan and the Musnads. Its summary: the Prophet (ﷺ), in one of his expeditions, was accompanied by his wife 'Aisha, the truthful, daughter of the truthful (Abu Bakr). Her necklace broke, so she was delayed searching for it. They loaded her camel and howdah, not realizing she was absent. Then the army set off, but she came to their place and knew that when they missed her they would return to her. They continued their journey. Safwan ibn al-Mu'attal al-Sulami, one of the excellent Companions (may Allah be pleased with him), had stayed behind at the rear of the people and slept; he saw 'Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her), recognized her, made his mount kneel, and she mounted it without either speaking to the other. Then he came leading her after the army had stopped at midday. When some of the hypocrites who were with the Prophet (ﷺ) on that journey saw Safwan bringing her in that state, they spread what they spread, and the report was circulated and taken up by tongues, until some believers were deceived by it and began passing these words around. Revelation was withheld from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for a long time, and after some time the news reached 'Aisha, and she grieved greatly. Then Allah revealed her innocence in these verses, admonished the believers, magnified this matter, and enjoined upon them beneficial instructions.

When some of the hypocrites who were with the Prophet (ﷺ) on that journey saw Safwan bringing her in that state, they spread what they spread, and the report was circulated and taken up by tongues, until some believers were deceived by it and began passing these words around. Revelation was withheld from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for a long time, and after some time the news reached 'Aisha, and she grieved greatly. Then Allah revealed her innocence in these verses, admonished the believers, magnified this matter, and enjoined upon them beneficial instructions.

{11} Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, those who came with the slander﴾, i.e., the monstrous lie, which is the accusation against the Mother of the Believers, ﴿are a faction among you﴾, i.e., a group affiliated with you, O assembly of believers. Among them is the believer who is truthful in his faith but was deceived by the propaganda of the hypocrites, and among them is the hypocrite. ﴿Do not think it bad for you; rather, it is good for you.﴾ This is because it contained the vindication and purity of the Mother of the Believers, the honouring of her mention, such that the general praise encompassed all the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ), and because it contained the clarification of verses that people need, and whose application will continue until the Day of Resurrection. All of this is a great good which would not have been realised were it not for the saying of the people of slander. When Allah wills a matter, He makes a cause for it. For this reason He addressed the discourse generally to all the believers, and informed them that the defaming of some of them by others is like defaming themselves. In this is the teaching that the believers, in their mutual affection, compassion, sympathy and unity for their common interests, are like one body, and the believer to the believer is like a building whose parts strengthen one another. Just as a person dislikes that anyone should defame his honour, so he should dislike that anyone should defame his believing brother who is as himself. If the servant does not reach this state, it is a sign of deficiency in his faith and of his lacking sincere counsel. ﴿For every person among them is what he has earned of sin.﴾ This is a warning to those who came with the slander that they will be punished for what they said, and the Prophet (ﷺ) indeed applied the prescribed punishment (hadd) to a group of them. ﴿And he who took upon himself its greater part﴾, i.e., the greater part of the slander, is the vile hypocrite Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, may Allah curse him. ﴿For him is a great punishment﴾, namely, eternal abiding in the lowest level of the Fire.

{12} Then Allah guided His servants upon hearing such speech, saying: ﴿Why, when you heard it, did the believing men and believing women not think good of their own kind?﴾, i.e., the believers should have thought well of one another, that they were safe from what was attributed to them, and that the faith they possess, which is known, repels the baseless slander against them. ﴿And say﴾ on account of that good opinion: ﴿Glory be to You﴾, i.e., exalting You above every evil, and far above Your testing Your chosen ones with such monstrous matters. ﴿This is a great calumny﴾, i.e., a lie and a fabrication, among the greatest and most evident of things. This is the good opinion obligatory upon the believer when he hears such speech about his believing brother: he should clear him with his tongue and deny the one who said it.

{13} ﴿Why did they not bring four witnesses for it?﴾, i.e., would that those who made the accusation had brought four witnesses for what they alleged, namely, four upright and acceptable men. ﴿Since they did not bring the witnesses, then they, in the sight of Allah, are the liars﴾. Even if they were themselves certain of it, they are liars in the judgement of Allah, for He forbade them to speak of it without four witnesses. For this reason He said ﴿in the sight of Allah﴾ and did not say simply ﴿they are the liars﴾. All of this is part of magnifying the sanctity of a Muslim's honour, such that it is not permitted to proceed to accuse him without the legal quorum of witnesses to its truth.

{14} ﴿Had it not been for the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy in this world and the Hereafter﴾, such that His kindness encompassed you in both, in matters of your religion and your worldly affairs, ﴿a great punishment would have touched you for what you plunged into﴾, i.e., what you engaged in, ﴿concerning the slander﴾, ﴿a great punishment﴾, because you deserved it for what you said. But by the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy, He prescribed repentance for you and made the punishment a means of purifying sins.

{15} ﴿When you received it with your tongues﴾, i.e., you took it up and passed it on to one another, and spread its news, and it was a false saying. ﴿And you said with your mouths what you had no knowledge of﴾. Both are forbidden: speaking falsehood and speaking without knowledge. ﴿And you thought it a trivial matter﴾, which is why some of the believers who later repented and purified themselves engaged in it. ﴿But it was, in the sight of Allah, great.﴾ This contains a strong warning against indulging in some sins with a disregard for them, for the servant gains nothing by his supposing them trivial. The sin does not lighten his punishment; rather, it multiplies the sin and makes it easy for him to commit it again.

{16} ﴿Why, when you heard it﴾, i.e., would that you, O believers, when you heard the speech of the people of slander, ﴿had said﴾, denouncing it and magnifying its gravity: ﴿It is not for us to speak of this﴾, i.e., it is not proper for us, nor fitting, to speak of this manifest slander, for the believer's faith prevents him from committing vile acts. ﴿This is a great slander﴾, i.e., a great lie.

{17} ﴿Allah admonishes you that you never return to the like of it﴾, i.e., to the like of accusing the believers of immorality. Allah admonishes you and advises you against it, and how excellent are the admonitions and advice of our Lord. It is therefore obligatory upon us to receive them with acceptance, submission, surrender, and gratitude to Him for what He has made clear to us. ﴿If you are believers.﴾ This shows that true faith prevents its possessor from proceeding to the forbidden things.

{18} ﴿And Allah makes clear to you the verses﴾, which contain the explanation of rulings, admonition, warning, encouragement and deterrence, He clarifies them for you in a manifest way. ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾, i.e., of perfect knowledge and comprehensive wisdom. From His knowledge and wisdom is that He taught you from His knowledge, and this is always in accordance with your interests at every time.

{19} ﴿Indeed, those who love that immorality should spread among the believers﴾, i.e., the monstrous and abominable matters, who love that the immorality should become known, ﴿will have a painful punishment﴾, i.e., one that pains the heart and the body. That is because of their deceit toward their Muslim brothers, their love of evil for them, and their audacity toward their honour. If this threat is for merely loving that immorality should spread and relishing it in the heart, then how about what is greater than that, namely, publicising it and transmitting it? Whether the immorality actually occurred or did not occur, all of this is from Allah's mercy toward His believing servants and His protection of their honour, just as He protected their blood and their wealth, and commanded them with what requires mutual affection, that each should love for his brother what he loves for himself and dislike for him what he dislikes for himself. ﴿And Allah knows, while you do not know﴾, and therefore He taught you and made clear to you what you are ignorant of.

{20} ﴿And had it not been for the bounty of Allah upon you﴾, which has encompassed you from every side, ﴿and His mercy﴾ upon you, ﴿and that Allah is Kind and Merciful﴾: were it not for His having made these rulings, admonitions and sublime wisdoms clear to you, and for His not having granted respite to those who opposed His command. But His bounty and His mercy, and that this is His inherent attribute, have caused you to receive worldly and otherworldly good that you cannot count or enumerate.

{21} Having forbidden this particular sin, He then forbade sins in general, saying: ﴿O you who believe, do not follow the footsteps of Satan﴾, i.e., his paths and his whisperings. The footsteps of Satan include all the sins connected with the heart, the tongue and the body.
From His wisdom, may He be exalted, is that He stated the ruling, which is the prohibition of following the footsteps of Satan, and the wisdom, which is the explanation of the evil in what is forbidden that compels and motivates its abandonment, saying: ﴿And whoever follows the footsteps of Satan, indeed, he commands immorality﴾, i.e., Satan commands what sound minds and the law regard as abominable among great sins, along with some souls' inclination toward it, ﴿and wrongdoing﴾, which is what reason rejects and does not recognise. The sins that are Satan's footsteps do not lie outside of this. Allah therefore forbade His servants from them as a blessing from Him upon them, that they should be thankful to Him and remember Him, for this is a protection for them from being defiled by vices and abominations. Among His kindness to them is that He forbade them from these, just as He forbade them from eating deadly poisons and the like. ﴿And had it not been for the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy, not one of you would ever have been purified﴾, i.e., none would have been cleansed from following the footsteps of Satan. This is because Satan, together with his army, strives to call to them and make them appealing, and the soul inclines to evil and commands it, deficiency controls the servant from all his directions, and faith is not strong. Were it left to these incitements, none would have been purified by cleansing from sins and evil deeds and growing through doing good deeds, for purification (zakah) includes both cleansing and growth. But His bounty and His mercy required that whoever among you has been purified should be purified. Among the supplications of the Prophet (ﷺ) was: "O Allah, grant my soul its piety, and purify it, for You are the best to purify it. You are its Guardian and its Lord." For this reason He said: ﴿But Allah purifies whom He wills﴾, i.e., whoever He knows will purify himself through purification. For this reason He said: ﴿And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.﴾

{22} ﴿And let not those of virtue and wealth among you swear not to give to the near of kin and the needy and the emigrants in the way of Allah; let them pardon and overlook﴾. Among those who engaged in the slander was Mistah ibn Uthathah, who was a relative of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him. Mistah was a poor emigrant in the way of Allah. Abu Bakr swore that he would not spend upon him, because of what he had said. Then this verse was revealed [forbidding him] from this oath, which implied cutting off support from him, and urging him to pardon and forgive, and promising him Allah's forgiveness if he forgave him. He said: ﴿Do you not love that Allah should forgive you? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, meaning: if you deal with His servants with pardon and forgiveness, He will deal with you in the same way. When Abu Bakr heard this verse, he said, "Yes, by Allah! I indeed love that Allah should forgive me," and he restored the support to Mistah.
This verse is evidence for the obligation of supporting a relative, and that support and kindness should not be abandoned because of a person's sin, and for urging pardon and forgiveness even if he committed what some criminals commit.

{23} Then He mentioned the severe threat against accusing chaste women, saying: ﴿Indeed, those who accuse chaste women﴾, i.e., those who are pure from immorality, ﴿heedless﴾, who have not even conceived of such a thing in their hearts, ﴿believing [women]: they are cursed in this world and the Hereafter﴾. This is in addition to the curse: it removes them far from His mercy and brings upon them the severity of His vengeance, and that punishment is on the Day of Resurrection.

{24} ﴿On the Day when their tongues, their hands and their feet will testify against them concerning what they used to do﴾. Every limb will testify against its owner to what it did. Allah, who made everything speak, will make them speak, and so he cannot deny it. Indeed, He was just with the servants in making their own selves their witnesses.

{25} ﴿On that Day, Allah will pay them their true due﴾, i.e., their recompense for their deeds, the true recompense that is based on justice and equity. They will find their recompense complete, having lost nothing of it. ﴿And they will say: "Woe to us! What is this Book that leaves neither a small nor a great thing but has counted it!" And they will find what they did present; and your Lord does not wrong anyone.﴾ ﴿And they will know﴾ at that great station ﴿that Allah is the manifest Truth﴾. They will know that the manifest truth is confined to Allah, the Exalted: His magnificent attributes are truth, His acts are truth, His worship is truth, meeting Him is truth, [His promise] and His threat are truth, His religious and retributive judgement is truth, and His messengers are truth. There is no truth except in Allah, and everything true is from Allah.

{26} ﴿Wicked women are for wicked men, and wicked men for wicked women﴾, i.e., every wicked man and woman, every wicked word and deed, is suited to what is wicked, agrees with it, accompanies it and resembles it. And every good man and woman, every good word and deed, is suited to what is good, agrees with it, accompanies it and resembles it. This is a general statement and a restriction admitting no exception. Among its most significant implications is that the prophets, especially the Messengers of firm resolve (Ulul-'Azm), and especially their master Muhammad (ﷺ), who is the best of the good creation without qualification, are suited only by every good woman. {12} Then Allah guided His servants upon hearing such speech, saying: ﴿Why, when you heard it, did the believing men and believing women not think good of their own kind?﴾, i.e., the believers should have thought well of one another, that they were safe from what was attributed to them, and that the faith they possess, which is known, repels the baseless slander against them. ﴿And say﴾ on account of that good opinion: ﴿Glory be to You﴾, i.e., exalting You above every evil, and far above Your testing Your chosen ones with such monstrous matters. ﴿This is a great calumny﴾, i.e., a lie and a fabrication, among the greatest and most evident of things. {14} ﴿Had it not been for the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy in this world and the Hereafter﴾, such that His kindness encompassed you in both, in matters of your religion and your worldly affairs, ﴿a great punishment would have touched you for what you plunged into﴾, i.e., what you engaged in, ﴿concerning the slander﴾, ﴿a great punishment﴾, because you deserved it for what you said. {20} ﴿And had it not been for the bounty of Allah upon you﴾, which has encompassed you from every side, ﴿and His mercy﴾ upon you, ﴿and that Allah is Kind and Merciful﴾: were it not for His having made these rulings, admonitions and sublime wisdoms clear to you, and for His not having granted respite to those who opposed His command. {14} ﴿Had it not been for the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy in this world and the Hereafter﴾, such that His kindness encompassed you in both, in matters of your religion and your worldly affairs, ﴿a great punishment would have touched you for what you plunged into﴾, i.e., what you engaged in, ﴿concerning the slander﴾, ﴿a great punishment﴾, because you deserved it for what you said. {18} ﴿And Allah makes clear to you the verses﴾, which contain the explanation of rulings, admonition, warning, encouragement and deterrence, He clarifies them for you in a manifest way. ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾, i.e., of perfect knowledge and comprehensive wisdom. {19} ﴿Indeed, those who love that immorality should spread among the believers﴾, i.e., the monstrous and abominable matters, who love that the immorality should become known, ﴿will have a painful punishment﴾, i.e., one that pains the heart and the body. {20} ﴿And had it not been for the bounty of Allah upon you﴾, which has encompassed you from every side, ﴿and His mercy﴾ upon you, ﴿and that Allah is Kind and Merciful﴾: were it not for His having made these rulings, admonitions and sublime wisdoms clear to you, and for His not having granted respite to those who opposed His command. {21} Having forbidden this particular sin, He then forbade sins in general, saying: ﴿O you who believe, do not follow the footsteps of Satan﴾, i.e., his paths and his whisperings. The footsteps of Satan include all the sins connected with the heart, the tongue and the body.

{25} ﴿On that Day, Allah will pay them their true due﴾, i.e., their recompense for their deeds, the true recompense that is based on justice and equity. {26} ﴿Wicked women are for wicked men, and wicked men for wicked women﴾, i.e., every wicked man and woman, every wicked word and deed, is suited to what is wicked, agrees with it, accompanies it and resembles it. {23} Then He mentioned the severe threat against accusing chaste women, saying: ﴿Indeed, those who accuse chaste women﴾, i.e., those who are pure from immorality, ﴿heedless﴾, who have not even conceived of such a thing in their hearts, ﴿believing [women]: they are cursed in this world and the Hereafter﴾. {24} ﴿On the Day when their tongues, their hands and their feet will testify against them concerning what they used to do﴾. Every limb will testify against its owner to what it did. {25} ﴿On that Day, Allah will pay them their true due﴾, i.e., their recompense for their deeds, the true recompense that is based on justice and equity. {26} ﴿Wicked women are for wicked men, and wicked men for wicked women﴾, i.e., every wicked man and woman, every wicked word and deed, is suited to what is wicked, agrees with it, accompanies it and resembles it. {11} Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, those who came with the slander﴾, i.e., the monstrous lie, which is the accusation against the Mother of the Believers, ﴿are a faction among you﴾, i.e., a group affiliated with you, O assembly of believers. In this is the teaching that the believers, in their mutual affection, compassion, sympathy and unity for their common interests, are like one body, and the believer to the believer is like a building whose parts strengthen one another. Just as a person dislikes that anyone should defame his honour, so he should dislike that anyone should defame his believing brother who is as himself. But by the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy, He prescribed repentance for you and made the punishment a means of purifying sins.

{15} ﴿When you received it with your tongues﴾, i.e., you took it up and passed it on to one another, and spread its news, and it was a false saying. ﴿And you said with your mouths what you had no knowledge of﴾. This is in addition to the curse: it removes them far from His mercy and brings upon them the severity of His vengeance, and that punishment is on the Day of Resurrection.

{24} ﴿On the Day when their tongues, their hands and their feet will testify against them concerning what they used to do﴾. Every limb will testify against its owner to what it did. Allah, who made everything speak, will make them speak, and so he cannot deny it. Indeed, He was just with the servants in making their own selves their witnesses.

{25} ﴿On that Day, Allah will pay them their true due﴾, i.e., their recompense for their deeds, the true recompense that is based on justice and equity. They will find their recompense complete, having lost nothing of it. ﴿And they will say: "Woe to us! What is this Book that leaves neither a small nor a great thing but has counted it!" And they will find what they did present; and your Lord does not wrong anyone.﴾ ﴿And they will know﴾ at that great station ﴿that Allah is the manifest Truth﴾. They will know that the manifest truth is confined to Allah, the Exalted: His magnificent attributes are truth, His acts are truth, His worship is truth, meeting Him is truth, [His promise] and His threat are truth, His religious and retributive judgement is truth, and His messengers are truth. There is no truth except in Allah, and everything true is from Allah.

{26} ﴿Wicked women are for wicked men, and wicked men for wicked women﴾, i.e., every wicked man and woman, every wicked word and deed, is suited to what is wicked, agrees with it, accompanies it and resembles it. And every good man and woman, every good word and deed, is suited to what is good, agrees with it, accompanies it and resembles it. This is a general statement and a restriction admitting no exception. Among its most significant implications is that the prophets, especially the Messengers of firm resolve (Ulul-'Azm), and especially their master Muhammad (ﷺ), who is the best of the good creation without qualification, are suited only by every good woman. Therefore, impugning ʿĀ'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, with this matter is an impugning of the Prophet (ﷺ), and this is the intended aim of the slander from the hypocrites' purpose. The very fact that she was the wife of the Messenger (ﷺ) shows that she could be none but good and pure of this vile matter. How much more so, when she is who she is: the sincere one among women, the best of them, the most knowledgeable of them, the purest of them, the beloved of the Messenger of the Lord of the worlds, in whose quilt, of all his wives, the revelation never descended upon him but hers!
Then He declared this explicitly, so that no room is left for the falsifier to speak, nor for doubt and suspicion any room: ﴿Those are cleared of what they say﴾. The reference is primarily to ʿĀ'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, and secondarily to the chaste, heedless believing women who follow her. ﴿For them is forgiveness﴾, covering all sins, ﴿and a noble provision﴾ in Paradise, proceeding from the Generous Lord.

{11} Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, those who came with the slander﴾, i.e., the monstrous lie, which is the accusation against the Mother of the Believers, ﴿are a faction among you﴾, i.e., a group affiliated with you, O assembly of believers. Among them is the believer who is truthful in his faith but was deceived by the propaganda of the hypocrites, and among them is the hypocrite. ﴿Do not think it bad for you; rather, it is good for you.﴾ This is because it contained the vindication and purity of the Mother of the Believers, the honouring of her mention, such that the general praise encompassed all the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ), and because it contained the clarification of verses that people need, and whose application will continue until the Day of Resurrection. All of this is a great good which would not have been realised were it not for the saying of the people of slander. When Allah wills a matter, He makes a cause for it. For this reason He addressed the discourse generally to all the believers, and informed them that the defaming of some of them by others is like defaming themselves. In this is the teaching that the believers, in their mutual affection, compassion, sympathy and unity for their common interests, are like one body, and the believer to the believer is like a building whose parts strengthen one another. Just as a person dislikes that anyone should defame his honour, so he should dislike that anyone should defame his believing brother who is as himself. If the servant does not reach this state, it is a sign of deficiency in his faith and of his lacking sincere counsel. ﴿For every person among them is what he has earned of sin.﴾ This is a warning to those who came with the slander that they will be punished for what they said, and the Prophet (ﷺ) indeed applied the prescribed punishment (hadd) to a group of them. ﴿And he who took upon himself its greater part﴾, i.e., the greater part of the slander, is the vile hypocrite Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, may Allah curse him. ﴿For him is a great punishment﴾, namely, eternal abiding in the lowest level of the Fire.

{12} Then Allah guided His servants upon hearing such speech, saying: ﴿Why, when you heard it, did the believing men and believing women not think good of their own kind?﴾, i.e., the believers should have thought well of one another, that they were safe from what was attributed to them, and that the faith they possess, which is known, repels the baseless slander against them. ﴿And say﴾ on account of that good opinion: ﴿Glory be to You﴾, i.e., exalting You above every evil, and far above Your testing Your chosen ones with such monstrous matters. ﴿This is a great calumny﴾, i.e., a lie and a fabrication, among the greatest and most evident of things. This is the good opinion obligatory upon the believer when he hears such speech about his believing brother: he should clear him with his tongue and deny the one who said it.

{13} ﴿Why did they not bring four witnesses for it?﴾, i.e., would that those who made the accusation had brought four witnesses for what they alleged, namely, four upright and acceptable men. ﴿Since they did not bring the witnesses, then they, in the sight of Allah, are the liars﴾. Even if they were themselves certain of it, they are liars in the judgement of Allah, for He forbade them to speak of it without four witnesses. For this reason He said ﴿in the sight of Allah﴾ and did not say simply ﴿they are the liars﴾. All of this is part of magnifying the sanctity of a Muslim's honour, such that it is not permitted to proceed to accuse him without the legal quorum of witnesses to its truth.

{14} ﴿Had it not been for the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy in this world and the Hereafter﴾, such that His kindness encompassed you in both, in matters of your religion and your worldly affairs, ﴿a great punishment would have touched you for what you plunged into﴾, i.e., what you engaged in, ﴿concerning the slander﴾, ﴿a great punishment﴾, because you deserved it for what you said. But by the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy, He prescribed repentance for you and made the punishment a means of purifying sins.

{15} ﴿When you received it with your tongues﴾, i.e., you took it up and passed it on to one another, and spread its news, and it was a false saying. ﴿And you said with your mouths what you had no knowledge of﴾. Both are forbidden: speaking falsehood and speaking without knowledge. ﴿And you thought it a trivial matter﴾, which is why some of the believers who later repented and purified themselves engaged in it. ﴿But it was, in the sight of Allah, great.﴾ This contains a strong warning against indulging in some sins with a disregard for them, for the servant gains nothing by his supposing them trivial. The sin does not lighten his punishment; rather, it multiplies the sin and makes it easy for him to commit it again.

{16} ﴿Why, when you heard it﴾, i.e., would that you, O believers, when you heard the speech of the people of slander, ﴿had said﴾, denouncing it and magnifying its gravity: ﴿It is not for us to speak of this﴾, i.e., it is not proper for us, nor fitting, to speak of this manifest slander, for the believer's faith prevents him from committing vile acts. ﴿This is a great slander﴾, i.e., a great lie.

{17} ﴿Allah admonishes you that you never return to the like of it﴾, i.e., to the like of accusing the believers of immorality. Allah admonishes you and advises you against it, and how excellent are the admonitions and advice of our Lord. It is therefore obligatory upon us to receive them with acceptance, submission, surrender, and gratitude to Him for what He has made clear to us. ﴿If you are believers.﴾ This shows that true faith prevents its possessor from proceeding to the forbidden things.

{18} ﴿And Allah makes clear to you the verses﴾, which contain the explanation of rulings, admonition, warning, encouragement and deterrence, He clarifies them for you in a manifest way. ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾, i.e., of perfect knowledge and comprehensive wisdom. From His knowledge and wisdom is that He taught you from His knowledge, and this is always in accordance with your interests at every time.

{19} ﴿Indeed, those who love that immorality should spread among the believers﴾, i.e., the monstrous and abominable matters, who love that the immorality should become known, ﴿will have a painful punishment﴾, i.e., one that pains the heart and the body. That is because of their deceit toward their Muslim brothers, their love of evil for them, and their audacity toward their honour. If this threat is for merely loving that immorality should spread and relishing it in the heart, then how about what is greater than that, namely, publicising it and transmitting it? Whether the immorality actually occurred or did not occur, all of this is from Allah's mercy toward His believing servants and His protection of their honour, just as He protected their blood and their wealth, and commanded them with what requires mutual affection, that each should love for his brother what he loves for himself and dislike for him what he dislikes for himself. ﴿And Allah knows, while you do not know﴾, and therefore He taught you and made clear to you what you are ignorant of.

{20} ﴿And had it not been for the bounty of Allah upon you﴾, which has encompassed you from every side, ﴿and His mercy﴾ upon you, ﴿and that Allah is Kind and Merciful﴾: were it not for His having made these rulings, admonitions and sublime wisdoms clear to you, and for His not having granted respite to those who opposed His command. But His bounty and His mercy, and that this is His inherent attribute, have caused you to receive worldly and otherworldly good that you cannot count or enumerate.

{21} Having forbidden this particular sin, He then forbade sins in general, saying: ﴿O you who believe, do not follow the footsteps of Satan﴾, i.e., his paths and his whisperings. The footsteps of Satan include all the sins connected with the heart, the tongue and the body.
From His wisdom, may He be exalted, is that He stated the ruling, which is the prohibition of following the footsteps of Satan, and the wisdom, which is the explanation of the evil in what is forbidden that compels and motivates its abandonment, saying: ﴿And whoever follows the footsteps of Satan, indeed, he commands immorality﴾, i.e., Satan commands what sound minds and the law regard as abominable among great sins, along with some souls' inclination toward it, ﴿and wrongdoing﴾, which is what reason rejects and does not recognise. The sins that are Satan's footsteps do not lie outside of this. Allah therefore forbade His servants from them as a blessing from Him upon them, that they should be thankful to Him and remember Him, for this is a protection for them from being defiled by vices and abominations. Among His kindness to them is that He forbade them from these, just as He forbade them from eating deadly poisons and the like. ﴿And had it not been for the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy, not one of you would ever have been purified﴾, i.e., none would have been cleansed from following the footsteps of Satan. This is because Satan, together with his army, strives to call to them and make them appealing, and the soul inclines to evil and commands it, deficiency controls the servant from all his directions, and faith is not strong. Were it left to these incitements, none would have been purified by cleansing from sins and evil deeds and growing through doing good deeds, for purification (zakah) includes both cleansing and growth. But His bounty and His mercy required that whoever among you has been purified should be purified. Among the supplications of the Prophet (ﷺ) was: "O Allah, grant my soul its piety, and purify it, for You are the best to purify it. You are its Guardian and its Lord." For this reason He said: ﴿But Allah purifies whom He wills﴾, i.e., whoever He knows will purify himself through purification. For this reason He said: ﴿And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.﴾

{22} ﴿And let not those of virtue and wealth among you swear not to give to the near of kin and the needy and the emigrants in the way of Allah; let them pardon and overlook﴾. Among those who engaged in the slander was Mistah ibn Uthathah, who was a relative of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him. Mistah was a poor emigrant in the way of Allah. Abu Bakr swore that he would not spend upon him, because of what he had said. Then this verse was revealed [forbidding him] from this oath, which implied cutting off support from him, and urging him to pardon and forgive, and promising him Allah's forgiveness if he forgave him. He said: ﴿Do you not love that Allah should forgive you? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, meaning: if you deal with His servants with pardon and forgiveness, He will deal with you in the same way. When Abu Bakr heard this verse, he said, "Yes, by Allah! I indeed love that Allah should forgive me," and he restored the support to Mistah.
This verse is evidence for the obligation of supporting a relative, and that support and kindness should not be abandoned because of a person's sin, and for urging pardon and forgiveness even if he committed what some criminals commit.

{23} Then He mentioned the severe threat against accusing chaste women, saying: ﴿Indeed, those who accuse chaste women﴾, i.e., those who are pure from immorality, ﴿heedless﴾, who have not even conceived of such a thing in their hearts, ﴿believing [women]: they are cursed in this world and the Hereafter﴾. Cursing is not imposed except for a grave sin, and He emphasised the curse by stating that it continues upon them in both abodes. ﴿And for them is a great punishment﴾. This is in addition to the curse: it removes them far from His mercy and brings upon them the severity of His vengeance, and that punishment is on the Day of Resurrection.

{24} ﴿On the Day when their tongues, their hands and their feet will testify against them concerning what they used to do﴾. Every limb will testify against its owner to what it did. Allah, who made everything speak, will make them speak, and so he cannot deny it. Indeed, He was just with the servants in making their own selves their witnesses.

{25} ﴿On that Day, Allah will pay them their true due﴾, i.e., their recompense for their deeds, the true recompense that is based on justice and equity. They will find their recompense complete, having lost nothing of it. ﴿And they will say: "Woe to us! What is this Book that leaves neither a small nor a great thing but has counted it!" And they will find what they did present; and your Lord does not wrong anyone.﴾ ﴿And they will know﴾ at that great station ﴿that Allah is the manifest Truth﴾. They will know that the manifest truth is confined to Allah, the Exalted: His magnificent attributes are truth, His acts are truth, His worship is truth, meeting Him is truth, [His promise] and His threat are truth, His religious and retributive judgement is truth, and His messengers are truth. There is no truth except in Allah, and everything true is from Allah.

{26} ﴿Wicked women are for wicked men, and wicked men for wicked women﴾, i.e., every wicked man and woman, every wicked word and deed, is suited to what is wicked, agrees with it, accompanies it and resembles it. And every good man and woman, every good word and deed, is suited to what is good, agrees with it, accompanies it and resembles it. This is a general statement and a restriction admitting no exception. Among its most significant implications is that the prophets, especially the Messengers of firm resolve (Ulul-'Azm), and especially their master Muhammad (ﷺ), who is the best of the good creation without qualification, are suited only by every good woman. Therefore, impugning ʿĀ'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, with this matter is an impugning of the Prophet (ﷺ), and this is the intended aim of the slander from the hypocrites' purpose. The very fact that she was the wife of the Messenger (ﷺ) shows that she could be none but good and pure of this vile matter. How much more so, when she is who she is: the sincere one among women, the best of them, the most knowledgeable of them, the purest of them, the beloved of the Messenger of the Lord of the worlds, in whose quilt, of all his wives, the revelation never descended upon him but hers!
Then He declared this explicitly, so that no room is left for the falsifier to speak, nor for doubt and suspicion any room: ﴿Those are cleared of what they say﴾. The reference is primarily to ʿĀ'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, and secondarily to the chaste, heedless believing women who follow her. ﴿For them is forgiveness﴾, covering all sins, ﴿and a noble provision﴾ in Paradise, proceeding from the Generous Lord.

{27} God instructs His believing servants not to enter houses other than their own without seeking permission, for in this there are several harms:

Among them is what the Messenger (ﷺ) mentioned when he said: "Permission to enter was only enjoined because of the sight." Thus, by neglecting it, the eye falls upon the private parts that are inside the houses, for the house, in covering what is behind it, is to a person like a garment in covering the nakedness of his body.

Another is that this brings suspicion from within, and one is accused of evil such as theft or other things, because entering stealthily indicates evil. God forbade the believers from entering houses other than their own {until you seek permission [tasta'nisu]}; that is, until you ask permission. He called seeking permission "istiʼnas" (seeking companionship), because through it companionship is achieved, and without it estrangement occurs. {And greet its occupants}: the manner of this is what came in the hadith: "Peace be upon you, may I enter?" {That}; that is, the mentioned seeking of permission, {is better for you, that you may remember} [24:27]: because it includes several benefits, and it is one of the obligatory noble morals. So if he is given permission, the one seeking permission enters.

{28} {And if you find no one in them}: then do not enter them {until permission is given to you. And if it is said to you, "Go back," then go back}; that is, do not refrain from returning and do not be angry about it, for the owner of the house has not withheld from you a right that is owed to you; rather, he is doing a favor. If he wills, he permits, or if he wills, he refuses, and you should not let arrogance or aversion seize any of you in this situation. {It is purer for you}; that is, more conducive to purifying you from misdeeds and increasing you in good deeds. {And God is Knowing of what you do} [24:28]: He will reward every doer for his deed, whether abundant or little, good or otherwise.

{29} This ruling applies to inhabited houses, whether or not they contain a person's belongings, and to uninhabited houses that contain no belongings of a person. As for houses in which their occupants are absent, which contain a person's belongings that he needs to enter, and in which there is no one from whom he can seek permission, such as rented houses and others, He mentioned them in His saying: {There is no blame upon you}; that is, no sin or wrongdoing. This indicates that entering without permission into the aforementioned houses is forbidden and sinful, {to enter uninhabited houses in which there are belongings for you} [24:29]. This is one of the wonderful exceptions of the Qur'an: His saying {Do not enter houses other than your own} is a general term for every house that is not owned by a person. God excluded from it the houses that are not His (owned) and in which there are a person's belongings and no occupant, thereby removing blame for entering them. {And God knows what you reveal and what you conceal} [24:29]: your outward and inward conditions, and He knows your interests; therefore He has legislated for you what you need and are compelled to of the legal rulings.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 24, verse 30:

{30} That is: guide the believers and say to them: those who have faith within them, which prevents them from falling into what undermines faith, {lower their gaze}: from looking at nakedness, at non-mahram women, and at beardless youths, whose gaze risks temptation, and at the adornments of this world that tempt and lead into what is forbidden. {And guard their private parts}: from unlawful intercourse, whether in the front or the back passage, or anything less than that, and from allowing them to be touched or looked at. {That}: the guarding of the gaze and the private parts {is purer for them}: more pure, more good, and more conducive to growth in their deeds. For whoever guards his private parts and his gaze is cleansed of the impurity with which the people of immorality defile themselves, and his deeds become pure through abandoning what is forbidden, which the soul desires and calls to. Whoever leaves something for the sake of God, God compensates him with something better than it. And whoever lowers his gaze from what is unlawful, God illuminates his insight. Moreover, when a servant guards his private parts and his gaze from what is unlawful, and from its preliminaries, despite the impulses of desire, his guarding of others is more effective; for this reason God called it "guarding" (ḥifẓ). A guarded thing, if its guardian does not strive to watch over it, to protect it, and to take the means that bring about its protection, will not be preserved. Likewise, if the servant does not strive to guard the gaze and the private parts, they will lead him into afflictions and trials.

And consider how He commanded the guarding of the private parts absolutely, because they are not permitted in any circumstance, whereas regarding the gaze He said: {lower some of their gaze} (min abṣārihim), using the particle min which indicates partiality, for looking is permissible in certain circumstances out of need, such as the gaze of a witness, a trader, a suitor, and the like. Then He reminded them of His knowledge of their deeds, so that they would strive to guard themselves from what is forbidden.

{31} When He commanded the believers to lower their gaze and guard their private parts, He commanded the believing women likewise, saying: ﴿And say to the believing women that they should lower their gaze﴾ from looking at private areas and at men with desire, and the like of forbidden looking. ﴿And guard their private parts﴾ from allowing intercourse with them, touching them, or looking at them unlawfully. ﴿And not reveal their adornment﴾ such as beautiful garments, jewelry, and the whole body, all of it being adornment. Since outer garments are necessary, He said: ﴿except what appears thereof﴾, i.e., the outer garments customarily worn, provided they do not invite temptation through them. ﴿And let them draw their head-coverings over their chests﴾ (juyub), and this is for complete concealment.

This indicates that the adornment whose display is forbidden includes the entire body, as we have mentioned.

Then He repeated the prohibition on displaying their adornment, to make an exception from it with His saying: ﴿except to their husbands﴾, i.e., their spouses, ﴿or their fathers, or the fathers of their husbands﴾, which includes the father himself and the grandfather however far up, ﴿or their sons, or the sons of their husbands﴾, which includes the sons, or the sons of the husbands however far down, ﴿or their brothers, or the sons of their brothers, or the sons of their sisters, or their women﴾, i.e., it is permissible for women to look at one another in general. It may be understood that the annexation (idafah) implies the female gender, i.e., Muslim women who are of their kind. This is evidence for those who say that a Muslim woman may not be seen unveiled by a dhimmi woman. ﴿Or what their right hands possess﴾: it is permissible for a female slave, if she is wholly owned by a woman, to look at her mistress as long as she wholly owns her; when ownership ends, wholly or partly, looking is not permissible. ﴿Or male attendants who have no physical desire﴾, i.e., [or] men who follow you and attach themselves to you and have no desire in this matter, such as the imbecile who does not understand such things, and the impotent man who has no desire left either in his private parts or in his heart; there is no prohibition on looking by such men. ﴿Or children who have not yet attained knowledge of women's private areas﴾, i.e., children below the age of discernment; it is permissible for them to look at non-related women. He, exalted is He, gave the reason as: they ﴿have not attained knowledge of women's private areas﴾, i.e., they have no knowledge of that, and desire has not yet arisen in them. This indicates that a woman must conceal herself from a child who has discernment, because he comes to know women's private areas.

﴿And let them not stamp their feet so as to reveal what they hide of their adornment﴾, i.e., they should not strike the ground with their feet so that the jewelry on them, such as anklets and others, makes a sound, so that their adornment becomes known because of it, which would become a means to temptation.

From this and similar texts is derived the principle of blocking means (sadd al-dhara'i'), that when a matter is permissible in itself but leads to something forbidden or is feared to lead to it, it is prohibited. Striking the foot on the ground is originally permissible, but since it becomes a means for the adornment to be known, it is forbidden.

When He, exalted is He, had commanded these good commands and enjoined these praiseworthy instructions, and since a believer must fall short in them, God commanded repentance, saying: ﴿And turn to God all together, O believers﴾, [because faith calls the believer to repentance]. Then He made success conditional upon it, saying: ﴿that you may succeed﴾. There is no path to success except through repentance, which is returning from what God dislikes, outwardly and inwardly, to what He loves, outwardly and inwardly. This indicates that every believer is in need of repentance, since God addressed the believers all together. It also contains encouragement to sincerity in repentance in His saying: ﴿And turn to God﴾, i.e., not for any purpose other than His countenance, such as seeking safety from worldly calamities, or showing off and seeking reputation, or similar corrupt aims.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 24, verse 32–33:

{32} Allah (Exalted) commands the guardians and masters to marry off those under their authority from among the ayama (the unmarried, i.e., those without spouses, men and women, whether previously married or virgins). It is therefore obligatory upon a relative or the guardian of an orphan to marry off whoever among those whose maintenance is obligatory upon him is in need of marriage. And if they are commanded to marry off those under their control, then their being commanded to marry themselves is all the more so (min bab awla).

{And the righteous among your male slaves and your female slaves}: It is possible that what is meant by "the righteous" is righteousness of religion, and that the righteous among the male and female slaves, who is the one who is not a debauched fornicator, is commanded by his master to be married as a reward for his righteousness and as an encouragement to him to remain so. And because the one corrupted by fornication is forbidden to marry, this supports what was mentioned at the beginning of the surah, that the marriage of a male fornicator and a female fornicator is forbidden until they repent. The specification of righteousness among slaves and female slaves, and not among free persons, is because such (corruption) is commonly found more among slaves.

It is also possible that what is meant by "the righteous" is those who are fit for marriage and are in need of it, from among the male and female slaves. This meaning is supported by the fact that the master is not commanded to marry off his slave before the slave's need for marriage. It is not far-fetched that both meanings are intended. And Allah knows best.

His saying: {If they are poor}; that is, the (prospective) spouses and those who marry, {Allah will enrich them out of His bounty}: so let not what you imagine deter you, namely that if one marries he becomes poor because of the large number of dependents and the like.

In this is an exhortation to marriage and a promise to the one who marries of wealth after poverty. {And Allah is All-Encompassing}: abundant in good, great in bounty. {All-Knowing}: of who deserves His bounty, religious and worldly or one of the two, from among those who do not deserve it; so He gives each what He knows and what His wisdom requires.

{33} {And let those who do not find the means to marry keep themselves chaste until Allah enriches them out of His bounty}: This is the ruling for the one unable to marry. Allah commanded him to be chaste: to restrain himself from what is forbidden and to take the means that restrain him from it, such as diverting the motives of his heart through thoughts that arise prompting him to fall into it. He should also do as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O young men! Whoever among you is able to marry, let him marry, and whoever is not able, let him fast, for it is a shield for him" (ba'ah, i.e., the capacity for marriage).

His saying: {those who do not find the means to marry}; that is, who are not able to marry, either because of their poverty, or the poverty of their guardians and masters, or their (guardians') refusal to marry them off, while they have no power to compel them to do so. This interpretation is better than the view of those who interpret it as "those who do not find the marriage payment (mahr)," and make the genitive complement stand in place of the thing it modifies. For in that there are two problems: first, ellipsis (hadhf) in the speech, while the original principle is the absence of ellipsis; and second, that the meaning becomes restricted to one who has two states: the state of wealth by his own means and the state of lack, thereby excluding slaves and female slaves and those whose marriage depends on their guardian, as we have mentioned. {Until Allah enriches them out of His bounty}: a promise to the one who keeps himself chaste that Allah will enrich him and make his affair easy, and a command to him to await relief, so that what he is in does not weigh heavily upon him.

His saying: {And those among your slaves who seek a deed of manumission, write it for them if you know good in them}; that is, whoever among your slaves seeks and asks for a deed of manumission (kitaba) to buy himself from his master, then respond to what he asks and write it for him. {If you know in them}; that is, among those seeking the writing, {good}; that is, capacity for earning and righteousness in his religion; because in the deed of manumission there is the attainment of two benefits: the benefit of emancipation and freedom, and the benefit of the payment he gives to ransom himself. Often he strives and exerts himself, and by the end of the term of the deed he may have gained for his master wealth that would not have been obtained while he was in bondage. So there is no harm to the master in writing it for him, along with the great benefit obtained by the slave. Therefore Allah commanded the writing of the deed in this manner as a command of obligation, as is apparent, or as a command of recommendation according to the other view. He also commanded assisting them in their manumission, because they are in need of that, since they have no wealth. So He said: {And give them from the wealth of Allah which He has given you}. This includes the command of the master who wrote the deed to give him from the payment or to waive part of it, and the command to people to help them. For this reason Allah assigned to those in manumission a share of zakat and encouraged giving it to them by saying: {from the wealth of Allah which He has given you}; that is, just as the wealth is Allah's wealth, and what is in your hands is only a gift from Allah to you and pure grace; so be good to the servants of Allah as Allah has been good to you.

The implication of this noble verse is that if the slave does not seek a deed of manumission, his master is not commanded to initiate writing it for him; and that if no good is known in him, by knowing the opposite of it: either that he knows he has no earnings, so that he becomes a burden upon people and wasted because of this; or that he fears that if he is freed and becomes in control of his own freedom he will be able to engage in corruption. In such a case he is not commanded to write the deed; rather he is forbidden from it, because of the prohibited consequence mentioned.

Then Allah (Exalted) said: {And do not compel your young women}; that is, your female slaves, {to prostitution}; that is, to become fornicators; {if they desire chastity}: for compulsion of them is conceivable only in this condition. As for when they do not desire chastity, they are then prostitutes whom their master must prevent from that. This prohibition is directed at what they used to practice in the Jahiliyyah, when the master would force his female slave into prostitution in order to take her earnings. Therefore He said: {in order to seek the goods of this worldly life}: it is not fitting for you that your female slaves be better than you and more chaste from fornication while you do that to them for the sake of the goods of this life, a little provision that appears and then passes away. Your gaining of dignity, cleanliness and honor, apart from the reward and punishment of the Hereafter, is better than your gaining of the little goods that bring you baseness and vileness.

Then He called the one who engaged in coercion to repentance, saying: {And whoever compels them, then indeed Allah, after their compulsion, is Forgiving and Merciful}: let him turn to Allah in repentance and desist from what he has done that angers Him. When he does that, Allah will forgive his sins and show him mercy, just as He showed mercy to himself by freeing it from punishment, and just as He showed mercy to his female slave by not compelling her to what harms her.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 24, verse 35:

{35} ﴿Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth﴾: the sensory and the immaterial. For He, may He be exalted, is Light in His essence, and His veil is Light, which, were He to unveil it, the glories of His Face would burn away everything within His creation that His sight reaches. By Him the Throne, the Footstool, the sun, the moon and the light were illuminated, and by Him Paradise was illuminated. Likewise, the immaterial light returns to Allah: His Book is light, His law is light, and faith and knowledge in the hearts of His messengers and His believing servants are light. Were it not for His light, darkness would pile up, and for this reason every place that loses His light, there is darkness and confinement. ﴿The likeness of His light﴾: that which guides to Him, namely the light of faith and the Qur'an in the hearts of the believers, ﴿is like a niche﴾; i.e., a recess (kuwwah) ﴿in which is a lamp﴾, because the recess gathers the light of the lamp so that it does not scatter. ﴿The lamp is in a glass, the glass﴾: by its clarity and brilliance, ﴿as if it were a star of brilliance﴾; i.e., shining with the luminosity of a pearl (durri), ﴿lit from a blessed tree, an olive﴾; i.e., lit from olive oil, whose flame is of the brightest kind, ﴿neither of the east﴾: exclusively, so that the sun does not reach it at the end of the day, ﴿nor of the west﴾: exclusively, so that the sun does not reach it [at the end of] the day. When both of these are negated, it is in a middle position of the earth, like the olives of Syria, which the sun reaches at the beginning and end of the day, so it becomes good, pure, and its oil is more clear. For this reason He said: ﴿its oil would almost glow﴾: from its purity, ﴿even if no fire touched it﴾. When fire touches it, it shines with a powerful brilliance. ﴿Light upon light﴾; i.e., the light of the fire and the light of the oil.

The aspect of this parable which Allah has struck, and its application to the state of the believer and the light of Allah in his heart, is that his innate nature (fitrah) upon which he was created is like pure oil; his nature is pure and prepared for divine teachings and lawful action. When knowledge and faith reach him, that light ignites in his heart like the ignition of fire in the wick of that lamp. He is pure of heart from wrong intention and wrong understanding concerning Allah; when faith reaches him, it shines with a great radiance because of its purity from impurities, and this is like the clarity of the pearl-like glass. Thus there gathers for him the light of nature, the light of faith, the light of knowledge, and the clarity of recognition: light upon light.

Since this is from the light of Allah, and not everyone is fit for it, He said: ﴿Allah guides to His light whom He wills﴾: from among those whom He knows to be pure and clean, and that he grows and flourishes with it. ﴿And Allah strikes parables for the people﴾: so that they may understand Him and comprehend, out of His kindness toward them and His benevolence to them, and so that truth becomes clear from falsehood; for parables bring intelligible meanings close to perceptible ones, so that the servants know them with clear knowledge. ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing of everything﴾: His knowledge encompasses all things. So know that His striking of parables is the striking of one who knows the realities of things and their details, and that they are a benefit to the servants; let your occupation be with reflecting upon them and understanding them, not with objecting to them or opposing them, for He knows and you do not know.

And since the light of faith and the Qur'an most often has its causes in the mosques, he mentioned them, extolling them, saying:

{36} That is: He is worshipped (Allah is worshipped) {in houses}: great and virtuous houses, which are the most beloved places to Him, namely the mosques. {Allah has permitted}; that is, He has commanded and enjoined {that they be raised and that His name be mentioned in them}. These two together comprise the rulings of the mosques. Included in "raising" them are their construction, sweeping and cleaning them of impurities and filth, and protecting them from the insane and children who do not guard against impurities, and from the disbeliever, and that they be safeguarded from idle talk within them and from raising voices for other than the remembrance of Allah. "And His name be mentioned in them" includes all prayer, obligatory and voluntary, the recitation of the Qur'an, glorification (tasbih), declaration of God's oneness (tahlil), and other kinds of remembrance, the learning and teaching of knowledge, studying together within them, i'tikaf (seclusion in worship), and other acts of worship performed in mosques. For this reason, the maintenance of mosques is of two kinds: the maintenance of construction and its upkeep, and the maintenance through the remembrance of Allah's name by prayer and other acts; and this is the nobler of the two kinds. For this reason, the five prayers and the Friday prayer were legislated in mosques, obligatory according to most scholars and recommended according to others.

{37} Then the Exalted praised its maintainers for their worship, saying: {He is glorified in it, in the mornings}, with sincerity, {by the dawn}: the beginning of the day, {and the evenings}: its end. {Men}: He specified these two times for their nobility and because travel toward Allah is facilitated and made easy in them. This includes glorification in prayer and otherwise. For this reason the morning and evening remembrances and their litanies were legislated for the morning and evening. That is: men glorify Allah in them, and what men they are! They are not among those who prefer worldly pleasures and trade and gainful occupations that distract them from their Lord. {Neither trade nor sale distracts them}: This encompasses every kind of earning that is sought for profit, so His saying {nor sale} is mentioned as the specific after the general (ʿatf al-khass ʿala al-ʿamm), because of the frequency of occupation with sale over other things. These men, even if they trade, sell and buy, there is no harm in that; but such dealings do not distract them by their giving them precedence and preference over {the remembrance of Allah, establishing prayer, and paying zakat}. Rather, they make obedience to Allah and His worship the ultimate goal of their aims and the final end of their purpose; whatever comes between them and it, they abandon.
Since leaving the world is difficult for most souls, and the love of gain through various kinds of trade is beloved to them, and it is generally hard for them to abandon it and they must make an effort to give precedence to the right of Allah over it, He mentioned what calls them to that, by encouragement and warning, saying: {They fear a day in which hearts and eyes will be turned about}: due to the severity of its terror and its unsettling of hearts and bodies. Therefore they feared that day, so acting and abandoning what distracts from it became easy for them.

{38} {That Allah may reward them the best of what they did}: What is meant by {the best of what they did} is their good, righteous deeds, because these are the best of what they did, since they also do permissible acts and others; reward is only given for good deeds. Like His saying, exalted is He: {That Allah may expiate from them the worst of what they did and reward them their due for the best of what they used to do} {And He increases them from His bounty}: a great increase beyond the recompense corresponding to their deeds. {And Allah provides for whom He wills without account}: rather, He gives him reward beyond what his deeds reach, and beyond what his hopes reach, and He gives him reward without counting or measuring. This is a metaphor for its great abundance.
