Rather, they make obedience to Allah and His worship the ultimate goal of their aims and the final end of their purpose; whatever comes between them and it, they abandon.
Since leaving the world is difficult for most souls, and the love of gain through various kinds of trade is beloved to them, and it is generally hard for them to abandon it and they must make an effort to give precedence to the right of Allah over it, He mentioned what calls them to that, by encouragement and warning, saying: {They fear a day in which hearts and eyes will be turned about}: due to the severity of its terror and its unsettling of hearts and bodies. Therefore they feared that day, so acting and abandoning what distracts from it became easy for them.

{38} {That Allah may reward them the best of what they did}: What is meant by {the best of what they did} is their good, righteous deeds, because these are the best of what they did, since they also do permissible acts and others; reward is only given for good deeds. Like His saying, exalted is He: {That Allah may expiate from them the worst of what they did and reward them their due for the best of what they used to do} {And He increases them from His bounty}: a great increase beyond the recompense corresponding to their deeds. {And Allah provides for whom He wills without account}: rather, He gives him reward beyond what his deeds reach, and beyond what his hopes reach, and He gives him reward without counting or measuring. This is a metaphor for its great abundance.

These are two examples which Allah struck for the deeds of the disbelievers, regarding their nullification and their going to waste, and the regret of those who did them. He said:

**Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on Surah 24, verses 39–40:**

{39} {And those who disbelieve}: in their Lord and who denied His messengers, {their deeds are like a mirage in a level desert}; i.e., in a plain where there is no tree and no vegetation. {The thirsty one thinks it to be water}: one who is extremely thirsty, who imagines what another would not imagine, due to the thirst he has. This supposition is false, yet he heads toward it to relieve his thirst. {Until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing}: so he regrets intensely, and his thirst increases because his hope has been cut off. Likewise, the deeds of the disbelievers are in the position of the mirage: they appear, and the ignorant person who does not understand matters thinks them to be beneficial deeds. Its appearance deceives him and its illusion beguiles him, and he too thinks them beneficial deeds for his desires. He also needs them, indeed he is compelled to them, like the thirsty one's need for water. {Until, when he comes to it [on the Day of Recompense], he finds it to be nothing}: he finds them lost, and the matter is that he has not been left either to his benefit or to his detriment, but rather {he finds Allah with him, and He pays him in full his account}: nothing of his deeds, be it a speck or a hair's breadth, is hidden from Him, and He will not withhold from him anything, little or much. {And Allah is swift in account}: so the ignorant should not consider that promise slow, for it must come to pass. Allah has likened their deeds to the mirage in a level desert, i.e., with no tree and no vegetation. This is an example of their hearts, in which there is no good and no righteousness, so that deeds would flourish in them. This is due to the preventing cause, which is disbelief.

{40} The second example of the invalidity of the disbelievers' deeds: {Like darkness in a deep sea}: whose bottom is far and whose extent is long, {covered by waves, above which are waves, above which are clouds, darkness upon darkness}: the darkness of the deep sea, then above it the darkness of the piled-up waves, then above that the darkness of the gloomy clouds, then above that the darkness of the pitch-black night. Thus the darkness intensified greatly, to the extent that one in that state, {when he extends his hand, he can hardly see it}: despite its closeness to him; how then would he see anything else? Likewise, the disbelievers have darkness piled upon their hearts: the darkness of nature, in which there is no good; above it the darkness of disbelief; above that the darkness of ignorance; and above that the darkness of the deeds proceeding from what has been mentioned. So they remain in darkness, bewildered, wandering blindly in their confusion, turning away from the straight path, and hesitating on the paths of error and misguidance. This is because Allah has forsaken them, and has not given them of His light. {And whoever Allah does not give light, for him there is no light}: because his soul is wrongdoing and ignorant, so there is in it no good and no light except what its Lord has given it and bestowed upon it.

It is possible that these two examples apply to the deeds of all the disbelievers, each of them fitting them, and He multiplied them for the multiplicity of attributes. It is also possible that each example is for a group and a category: the first is for the leaders who are followed, and the second is for the followers. And Allah knows best.

God has inspired it with that prayer and glorification, either through the messengers, as with the jinn, humankind and the angels, or through inspiration from Him, exalted is He, as with the rest of the creatures.

This second possibility is the more probable, as shown by His words: {And God is Knowing of what they do}; that is, He knows all of their actions, and nothing of them is hidden from Him, and He will recompense them for that. Thus, on this reading, He has combined their knowledge of their deeds, which comes through His teaching them, with His own knowledge of their deeds, which implies recompense. Thereby the pools are filled, the streams gush forth, the valleys flow, and the earth brings forth every beautiful pair. At times Allah sends down from that cloud hail which destroys whatever it strikes, {He strikes with it whom He wills and averts it from whom He wills}; i.e., according to what His decreed judgment and His wisdom, for which He is praised, require. {The flash of its lightning nearly} (yakādu sanā barqihi), i.e., the light of the lightning of that cloud, because of its intensity, nearly {takes away the sight} (yadhhabu bil-abṣār). Is not He who originated them, drove them to His needy servants, and sent them down in a manner by which benefit is achieved and harm is removed, the One of complete power, of executed will, and of vast mercy?

{44} {Allah turns the night and the day} (yuqallibu Allahu al-layla wal-nahar): from heat to cold, from cold to heat, from night to day, and from day to night, and He alternates the days among His servants. {Indeed in that is a lesson for those of vision} (li-ulī al-abṣār); i.e., for those possessing insight and penetrating intellects, which perceive the matters sought from them just as eyes perceive visible, sensory matters. The discerning person looks at these creatures with a look of consideration, reflection, and contemplation of what they were intended for and from them, whereas the heedless, ignorant one who turns away looks at them with a look of heedlessness, like the gaze of cattle.

{45} He draws His servants' attention to what they witness: that He created all the moving creatures upon the face of the earth "from water"; that is, their basic substance is entirely water, as the Most High said: ﴿And We made from water every living thing﴾. The animals that reproduce by mating have as their substance the water of the sperm-drop when the male impregnates the female. Animals that are generated from the earth, such as insects, come into being only from watery moisture; nothing of them is ever generated without water. The substance is one, but the creation differs in many respects. "Among them is that which walks on its belly": such as the snake and the like. "And among them is that which walks on two legs": such as human beings and many birds. "And among them is that which walks on four": such as the grazing livestock and the like. Their diversity, although the origin is one, indicates the all-encompassing power of God's will and the comprehensiveness of His ability. For this reason He said: ﴿God creates what He wills﴾; that is, of creatures, with the attributes He wills. ﴿Indeed, God is over all things competent﴾; just as He sends down rain upon the earth, which is one impregnation, and the mother is one, namely the earth, yet the offspring are of differing kinds and qualities. ﴿And on the earth are neighboring tracts, and gardens of grapevines, and crops, and palm trees, some multi-stemmed and some single-stemmed, watered with one water, yet We favor some of them over others in fruit. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reason.﴾

{46} That is: We have shown mercy to Our servants and sent down to them clear verses, meaning verses evident in their indication of all the legislative aims, praiseworthy manners and sound knowledge. Thereby the paths became manifest, and right guidance was distinguished from error, and guidance from misguidance. No slightest doubt remained for the falsifier to cling to, nor the slightest difficulty for one who seeks what is correct, because they are a revelation from One whose knowledge is perfect, whose mercy is perfect, and whose clarification is perfect; so there is no clarification after His clarification. Thereafter, whoever perishes, perishes after clear proof, and whoever lives, lives after clear proof. ﴿And Allah guides whom He wills﴾ from among those for whom the good outcome and the foot of truthfulness have preceded ﴿to a straight path﴾; that is, a clear, direct path that leads to Him and to the abode of His honour, including knowledge of the truth, preferring it, and acting upon it. He made the complete clarification general for all creation, and specified guidance for whom He wills. This is His bounty and His kindness, and the bounty of the Generous is not something to be reckoned upon. And that is His justice, and He has cut off the argument of the one who argues. And Allah knows best where to place His kindness.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 24, verses 47–50:

{47} He, the Exalted, informs us about the state of the wrongdoers, those in whose hearts is a disease, weakness of faith, hypocrisy, doubt and feebleness. He knows that they say with their tongues and profess belief in God and obedience, but then they do not act upon what they have said, and a group of them turn away from obedience with great aversion. The proof is His saying: {and they are turning away}. For one who turns away may still have the intention of returning to what he turned away from, whereas this one who turns away is averse, giving no attention and no consideration to what he has turned away from. You will find this state matching the condition of many who claim faith and obedience to God while their faith is weak. You will find them not performing many acts of worship, especially those acts that are hard on many souls, such as zakat, obligatory and voluntary expenditure, jihad in the way of God, and the like.

{48} {And when they are called to God and His Messenger, that he may judge between them}: that is, when there arises a dispute between them and someone else, and they are called to [the judgment of] God and His Messenger, {behold, a party of them turn away}. They desire the judgments of the Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance before Islam) and prefer the judgments of man-made laws that are not in accordance with the Sharia over the judgments of the Sharia, because they know that the right is against them, and that the Sharia judges only by what corresponds to reality.

{49} {But if the right is theirs, they come to him willingly}: that is, to the judgment of the Sharia {willingly}. That is not because it is a Sharia judgment, but only because it agrees with their desires. They are not praised in this state, even if they come to it willingly, because the servant in truth is one who follows the truth in what he loves and dislikes, and in what pleases him and what saddens him. As for one who follows the Sharia when it agrees with his desire and abandons it when it opposes him, and puts his desire before the Sharia, he is not a servant in the true sense.

{50} God said, rebuking them for turning away from the Sharia judgment: {Is there a disease in their hearts?}: that is, an ailment that has taken the heart out of its soundness and removed its perception, so that it becomes like the sick person who turns away from what benefits him and turns toward what harms him. {Or do they have doubt?}: that is, they doubt, and their hearts are troubled about the judgment of God and His Messenger, and they accuse Him of not judging with truth. {Or do they fear that God and His Messenger will deal unjustly with them?}: that is, that He will judge against them with an oppressive, tyrannical judgment. Yet this is only their own description; {rather, they are the wrongdoers}. As for the judgment of God and His Messenger, it is in the utmost justice and equity and in accord with wisdom. {And who is better in judgment than God for a people who are certain?}

In these verses there is evidence that faith is not merely speech unaccompanied by action. For this reason He negated faith from those who turned away from obedience and from the obligation to submit to the judgment of God and His Messenger in every circumstance. Whoever does not submit to it indicates a disease in his heart and doubt in his faith. It is also forbidden to think ill of the rulings of the Sharia, or to suppose that they contain what opposes justice and wisdom.

When he had mentioned the state of those who turn away from the Sharia judgment, he mentioned the state of the praiseworthy believers, saying:

{50} God said, rebuking them for turning away from the Sharia judgment: {Is there a disease in their hearts?}: that is, an ailment that has taken the heart out of its soundness and removed its perception, so that it becomes like the sick person who turns away from what benefits him and turns toward what harms him. {Or do they have doubt?}: that is, they doubt, and their hearts are troubled about the judgment of God and His Messenger, and they accuse Him of not judging with truth. {Or do they fear that God and His Messenger will deal unjustly with them?}: that is, that He will judge against them with an oppressive, tyrannical judgment. Yet this is only their own description; {rather, they are the wrongdoers}. As for the judgment of God and His Messenger, it is in the utmost justice and equity and in accord with wisdom. {And who is better in judgment than God for a people who are certain?}

In these verses there is evidence that faith is not merely speech unaccompanied by action. For this reason He negated faith from those who turned away from obedience and from the obligation to submit to the judgment of God and His Messenger in every circumstance. Whoever does not submit to it indicates a disease in his heart and doubt in his faith. It is also forbidden to think ill of the rulings of the Sharia, or to suppose that they contain what opposes justice and wisdom.

When he had mentioned the state of those who turn away from the Sharia judgment, he mentioned the state of the praiseworthy believers, saying:

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 24, verses 51–52:

{51} That is: {The only saying of the believers}, truly, those who confirm their faith by their deeds, when they are called {to Allah and His Messenger, that he may judge between them}, whether the ruling agrees with their desires or opposes them, {is that they say: "We hear and we obey."} That is: we hear the ruling of Allah and His Messenger, we answer the one who calls us to it, and we obey with complete obedience free from any reluctance. {And those are the successful}: He restricted success to them, because success is attaining what is sought and being saved from what is disliked. None achieves success except one who makes Allah and His Messenger the judge and obeys Allah and His Messenger.

{52} Having mentioned the excellence of obedience in judgment specifically, He mentioned its excellence in general, in all circumstances, saying: {And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger}: by confirming their report and carrying out their command, {and fears Allah}; that is, fears Him with a fear joined with knowledge, so that he abandons what He has forbidden and restrains himself from what he desires. For this reason He said: {and is mindful of Him}: by abandoning what is prohibited, because taqwa (God-consciousness, mindfulness of Allah), when mentioned alone, includes both doing what is commanded and abandoning what is forbidden, and when it is joined with birr (righteousness) or ta'ah (obedience), as in this place, it is explained as guarding oneself against the punishment of Allah by abandoning His disobedience. {Those are}: those who combined obedience to Allah and obedience to His Messenger, and fear of Allah and taqwa of Him, {they are the victorious}: through their deliverance from punishment, since they abandoned its causes, and their attainment of reward, since they did its causes. Thus victory is restricted to them. As for one who does not possess their qualities, he loses from victory in proportion to what he falls short of these praiseworthy attributes.

This verse includes the right shared between Allah and His Messenger, which is obedience, which necessarily entails faith; the right specific to Allah, which is fear and taqwa; and there remains the third right specific to the Messenger, which is ta'zir (honouring and supporting) and tawqir (reverence), just as He combined the three rights in Surah al-Fath in His saying: {that you may believe in Allah and His Messenger, and support him and honour him, and glorify Him morning and evening}.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 24, verses 53–54:

{53} He, exalted is He, informs us about the state of those among the hypocrites who stayed behind from the Messenger ﷺ in jihad, and those in whose hearts is a disease and weakness of faith, that they swear by God: {If you commanded them, they would surely go out}: regarding what is yet to come, or {if you had indicated to them when you went out}. The first meaning (is) more preferable. God said, refuting them: {Say, "Do not swear; obedience is known."} That is: we have no need of your oaths or your excuses, for God has informed us of your news. Your obedience is well known and is not hidden from us. We already knew from you sluggishness and laziness without any excuse. So there is no basis for your excuse and your oath. Such matters are needed only by one whose situation is ambiguous and whose state is unclear; for such a person an excuse may bring him acquittal. As for you, (it is) certainly not (so), and (it is) not yet (the time for excuses). Rather, you are awaited and feared for, lest the punishment and vengeance of God descend upon you. For this reason He threatened them with His words: {Indeed, God is Aware of what you do}: and He will repay you for it in the fullest recompense.

{54} This is their state in reality. As for the Messenger, upon him be prayer and peace, his duty is to command you and forbid you. For this reason He said: {Say, "Obey God and obey the Messenger. But if you turn away"}: if you comply, it will be your good fortune and your happiness; and if you {turn away, then upon him is only that with which he has been entrusted}: of the message, and he has conveyed it; {and upon you is that with which you have been entrusted}: of obedience, and your state has become clear and manifest. Thus your misguidance, your error, and your deserving of punishment have become evident. {And if you obey him, you will be guided}: to the straight path in speech and action. There is no way for you to be guided except by obeying him; without that it is not possible, rather it is impossible. {And the Messenger's duty is only clear notification}: that is, your clear notification that leaves no doubt or ambiguity for anyone. He, upon him be prayer and peace, has done so; he delivered the clear message. It is God, exalted is He, Who will hold you to account and repay you. The Messenger has no share in the matter, and he has fulfilled his duty.

This is one of God's true promises, whose fulfilment and reality have been witnessed. He promised those among this community who hold to faith and righteous deeds that He would make them successors (khulafa') on the earth, and that they would be the ones who hold authority over its management. He also promised that He would establish for them ﴿their religion which He has approved for them﴾, which is the religion of Islam, the one that surpasses all other religions. He approved it for this community because of its excellence, its nobility, and His favour upon it, by enabling them to establish it and its laws, both outward and inward, in themselves and in others. Other religious communities and all disbelievers would be subdued and humiliated. He also promised that He would replace their fear with [security] ﴿after their fear﴾. Before this, each of them could not show his religion or practise what he held except by suffering much harm from the disbelievers. The Muslim community was also very small compared to others, and the people of the earth had shot at them with one bow and plotted harm against them. God promised them these matters at the time the verse was revealed, and they had not yet witnessed succession on the earth, empowerment in it, the establishment of the Islamic religion, or complete security, such that they would worship God without associating anything with Him and fear no one but God.

The early generations of this community then held to faith and righteous deeds to a degree that surpassed others. So God empowered them over the lands and their peoples, the eastern and western regions of the earth were opened, and complete security and complete authority were achieved. This is among God's wondrous and dazzling signs. The matter will continue until the Hour arrives, as long as they hold to faith and righteous deeds. What God promised them must necessarily come to pass. God only lets disbelievers and hypocrites overpower them at times, and causes them to be defeated, because Muslims have neglected faith and righteous deeds.

﴿And whoever disbelieves after that﴾: after this empowerment and complete dominion granted to you, O assembly of Muslims. ﴿Those are the defiantly disobedient﴾: those who have departed from obedience to God and become corrupt, so they are not fit for any good and have no capacity for goodness. The one who abandons faith in a time of his might and dominance, when there are no barriers preventing him from it, shows the corruption of his intention and the wickedness of his inner self, for he has no reason to abandon religion except that.

This verse indicates that God has empowered those before us and made them successors on the earth, as Moses said to his people: ﴿He will make you successors in the land, and see how you act﴾. And the Exalted said: ﴿We wished to bestow favour upon those who were oppressed in the land, and to make them leaders and make them the inheritors, and to establish them in the land﴾.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 24, verses 56–57:

{56} God, exalted is He, commands the establishment of the ṣalāh (prayer) with its pillars, conditions and etiquette, outwardly and inwardly, and the giving of the zakāh (obligatory almsgiving) from the wealth over which God has made His servants vicegerents and which He has given them. This is by giving it to the poor and to the others whom God named as recipients of zakāh. These two are the greatest and most exalted acts of obedience, combining the right of Him and the right of His creation: sincerity toward the One worshipped and kindness toward His servants. Then He joined to them a general command, saying: ﴿And obey the Messenger﴾. This means carrying out his commands and avoiding his prohibitions. ﴿And whoever obeys the Messenger has indeed obeyed God﴾. ﴿That you may be shown mercy﴾: when you do this. Whoever wants mercy, this is its path. Whoever hopes for it without establishing the ṣalāh, giving the zakāh and obeying the Messenger is a deluded liar, and his soul has deceived him with false wishes.

{57} ﴿Do not think that those who disbelieve can escape [Allah] within the land﴾. Do not be deceived by what they are given enjoyment of in the life of this world, for God, although He gives them respite, does not neglect them. ﴿We grant them enjoyment for a little; then We will force them to a severe punishment﴾. Therefore He said here: ﴿And their refuge is the Fire, and wretched is the destination﴾; that is, wretched is the final abode of the disbelievers: the abode of evil, regret and everlasting punishment.

{58} Allah commanded the believers that their slaves (mamalik) and those among their children who have not yet reached puberty (al-hulum) should seek permission from them. Allah has mentioned His wisdom in this, namely that there are three times of nakedness (awrat) for which permission is to be sought: the time of their sleep at night after the night prayer (al-'isha'), and at the time of their waking before the dawn prayer (salat al-fajr). This is because, generally, a sleeper uses, for sleeping at night, a garment other than his usual garment. As for daytime sleep, since it was generally brief, a servant may sleep in it in his ordinary clothes, so Allah restricted it by His saying: ﴿and when you put off your clothes at midday﴾; that is, for the midday rest (al-qa'ila) in the middle of the day. Thus, in these three situations, slaves and young children are like others: they are not allowed to enter except with permission. As for other than these three times, He said: ﴿there is no blame on you or on them beyond these﴾; that is, they are not like others, for they are needed constantly, so it would be burdensome to seek permission from them at every time. For this reason He said: ﴿they go about among you, some of you attending upon others﴾; that is, they frequent you in the conduct of your affairs and needs. ﴿Thus Allah makes the signs clear to you﴾: a clarification joined with His wisdom, so that it may be firmly established, strengthened, and so that by it one may know the mercy and wisdom of the Lawgiver. For this reason He said: ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾: He has all-encompassing knowledge of the obligatory, the impossible, and the possible, and wisdom which places everything in its proper place; He gave every creature its appropriate creation, and gave every legal ruling its fitting judgment, including these rulings which He has made clear, along with their sources (ma'akhidh) and their goodness.

{59} ﴿And when the children among you reach puberty (al-hulum)﴾: that is, the emission of semen (al-maniy), whether while awake or in a dream. ﴿then let them seek permission as those before them sought permission﴾; that is, at all times. Those before them are those whom Allah mentioned in His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, do not enter houses other than your own until you have asked permission and greeted their occupants...﴾ (the verse). ﴿Thus Allah makes clear to you His signs﴾: He explains them and details their rulings. ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.﴾

In these two verses there are benefits:

Among them: the master and the guardian of a child are both addressed with the duty of teaching their slaves, and those under their guardianship among the children, religious knowledge and etiquette; because Allah directed the address to them by His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, let those whom your right hands possess and those among you who have not reached puberty seek permission from you...﴾ (the verse). This cannot be achieved except through teaching and discipline, and by His saying: ﴿There is no blame on you or on them beyond these﴾.

Among them: the command to guard the awrat and to take precaution in this in every respect, and that the place and location where a person's nakedness is likely to be seen is forbidden for bathing in, for cleaning oneself (istinja'), and the like.

Among them: the permissibility of uncovering the awrat out of need, such as the need during sleep, during urination and defecation, and the like.

Among them: that the Muslims were accustomed to the midday rest (al-qayla) in the middle of the day, just as they were accustomed to sleeping at night; because Allah addressed them by describing their existing condition.

Among them: that a child who has not yet reached puberty may not be permitted to see the awrat, and his awrat may not be seen; because Allah did not command seeking permission from them except for a matter that is not permissible.

Among them: that a slave also may not see the awrat of his master, just as his master may not see his awrat, as we mentioned concerning the child.

Among them: that the preacher, the teacher, and others who speak on matters of religious knowledge should join the ruling with an explanation of its source (ma'khadh) and basis, and not present it bare of evidence and reasoning; because when Allah explained the aforementioned ruling, He gave its reason by His saying: ﴿three times of nakedness for you﴾.

Among them: that the young child and the slave are both addressed, just as their guardian is addressed; by His saying: ﴿there is no blame on you or on them beyond these﴾.

Among them: that the saliva of a child is pure, even if it comes after an impurity such as vomit; by the Most High's saying: ﴿they go about among you﴾; together with the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ), when he was asked about the cat: "It is not impure; it is among those who go about among you, male and female."

Among them: the permissibility of a person employing children under his authority in a customary manner that does not burden the child; by His saying: ﴿they go about among you﴾. Among them: that the detailed ruling mentioned applies only to those below puberty, whereas for those who have reached puberty, there is only seeking permission.

Among them: that puberty is attained by emission, so every legal ruling tied to puberty is attained by emission; this is agreed upon, and the only disagreement is whether puberty is attained by age or by the growth of pubic hair (al-'ana).

And Allah knows best.

{60} {And as for women past child-bearing}, meaning those who have ceased to desire marriage and sexual pleasure, {who have no hope of marriage}, meaning they do not aspire to marriage and no one aspires to them, either because she is an old woman with no desire, or because she is of unattractive appearance, not desired and not desiring. {There is no blame upon them}, meaning no sin or wrongdoing, {if they put off their outer garments}, meaning the outer clothing such as the head-covering and the like, concerning which Allah said to women: {and let them draw their head-coverings over their bosoms}. For such women it is permissible to uncover their faces, since the harm feared from them and from others is safe.

Since the removal of blame from them regarding the laying aside of clothing might lead one to suppose that it is permissible for them to use it for anything at all, he averted this misconception by his words: {without displaying adornment}, meaning without showing people any adornment of beautification through outer garments, and while still covering her face; and without striking their feet together so as to reveal what they conceal of their adornment. For the mere presence of adornment on a woman, even if she is covered and even if she is not desired, can become a source of temptation and place the one who looks upon her in a state of sin. {But that they refrain is better for them}: "Abstaining" (al-isti'faf) means seeking chastity by adopting the means that bring it about, such as marriage and abandoning what may lead to temptation. {And Allah is All-Hearing}, of all sounds. {All-Knowing}, of intentions and purposes; so let them beware of every corrupt speech and intention, and let them know that Allah will recompense them for it.

{61} He, Exalted is He, informs of His favour upon His servants, and that He has not placed upon them any hardship in the religion, but has made it easy in the utmost degree of ease. He said: ﴿There is no blame upon the blind, nor upon the lame, nor upon the sick [for not going out to fight]﴾. That is: there is no sin upon these in abandoning the obligatory matters that depend upon one of them, such as jihad and the like, which depend on the sight of the blind, the soundness of the lame, or the health of the sick. For this general meaning that we have mentioned, He stated the matter in unrestricted terms and did not qualify it, as He qualified His saying: ﴿nor upon yourselves﴾, that is, any hardship, ﴿that you eat from your houses﴾, that is, the houses of your children. This accords with the established hadith: "You and your wealth belong to your father," and the other hadith: "Indeed the best of what you eat is from your earnings, and indeed your children are from your earnings."

The intended meaning of His saying ﴿from your houses﴾ is not a person's own house, for that would be a case of obtaining what is already obtained (tahsil al-hasil), which the speech of God is exalted above. Moreover, it is the negation of hardship concerning what might be suspected or imagined to involve sin from those mentioned; as for a person's own house, there is no slightest suspicion in it. ﴿Or the houses of your fathers, or the houses of your mothers, or the houses of your brothers, or the houses of your sisters, or the houses of your paternal uncles, or the houses of your paternal aunts, or the houses of your maternal uncles, or the houses of your maternal aunts﴾: these are well known. ﴿Or that whose keys you possess﴾, that is, the houses over which you have authority by agency, guardianship, or the like. As for interpreting it as "the slave," this is not sound, for two reasons. The first: a slave is not described by saying "you possess his keys"; rather one says "what you own" or "what your right hands possess," since they own him entirely, not merely his keys. The second: the houses of slaves are not separate from a person's own house, since the slave and what he owns belong to his master, so there is no basis for negating hardship in that case. ﴿Or your friend﴾. This negated hardship regarding eating from these houses applies entirely when it is without permission. The wisdom in this is known from the context: these named persons have, by custom and common usage, been accustomed to leniency in eating from such houses, on account of close kinship, complete authority, or friendship. Were it supposed that any of these lacked such leniency and were stingy regarding the said eating, it would not be permissible to eat and the hardship would not be lifted, in view of the wisdom and purpose. As for His saying ﴿There is no blame upon you that you eat together or separately﴾, all of that is permissible: the members of one household eating together, or each one of them eating alone. This is the negation of hardship, not the negation of virtue; otherwise, gathering for the meal is more excellent. ﴿So when you enter houses﴾: an indefinite noun in a conditional context, encompassing one's own house and the house of others, whether or not there is a resident in the house. So when a person enters it, ﴿then greet one another﴾, that is, let some of you greet others, because the Muslims are, by their mutual affection, mercy, and compassion, as though they were one person. Greeting is prescribed for entering all houses, without distinction between one house and another; and it was previously mentioned that seeking permission has detailed rulings. Then He praised this greeting, saying: ﴿a greeting from God, blessed and good﴾, that is, your greeting by your saying: "Peace be upon you, and the mercy of God and His blessings," or: "Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of God," when you enter the houses, ﴿a greeting from God﴾, that is, He has prescribed it for you and made it your greeting. ﴿Blessed﴾: for it includes safety from deficiency and the attainment of mercy, blessing, growth, and increase. ﴿Good﴾: for it is among the good words beloved to God, which bring gladness of heart to the one greeted, love, and the drawing of affection.

When He had explained these sublime rulings to us, He said: ﴿Thus God makes clear to you the verses﴾, that is, the signs indicating His legal rulings and their wisdoms, ﴿that you may understand﴾ from Him, so that you comprehend and understand them with your hearts, and that you may be among the people of sound intellect and discerning minds. Knowledge of His legal rulings in their proper form increases the intellect and the mind grows through it, because their meanings are the most noble meanings and their etiquettes the most noble etiquettes; and because recompense is of the same kind as the deed: just as one used one's intellect to understand from one's Lord and to reflect upon His signs to which He called, He increases one in that.

In these verses there is evidence for a general universal principle: that custom and common usage specify the meaning of expressions, just as a word specifies another word. The original rule is that a person is forbidden to take the food of another, yet God permitted eating from the houses of these persons on account of custom and common usage. Therefore, every matter that depends on the permission of the owner of a thing, when his permission is known by speech or by custom, it is permissible to proceed with it.

Also in them: evidence that a father may take and possess from his child's wealth what does not harm the child, because God called His house "a house" for a person.

Also in them: evidence that one who manages a person's house, such as his wife, his sister, and the like, may by custom eat from it and feed the customary beggar.

Also in them: evidence for the permissibility of sharing in food, whether they eat gathered together or separately, even if this leads to some of them eating more than others.

**Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on Surah 24, verses 62–64:**

{62} This is guidance from God to His believing servants: when they are with the Messenger (ﷺ) in a matter that requires gathering, that is, one that necessarily or beneficially requires that they all be present, such as jihad, consultation, and similar affairs in which the believers share, then the public interest requires that they gather for it and not disperse. The one who truly believes in God and His Messenger does not leave for any matter, does not return to his family, and does not go off to attend to some personal need that takes him away from them, except with the permission of the Messenger or of his deputy after him. God made the requirement of faith to be not leaving except with permission. He praised them for this act and for their good manners toward His Messenger and toward the leader among them, saying: ﴿Indeed, those who ask your permission are the ones who believe in God and His Messenger.﴾ But will he grant them permission or not? He mentioned two conditions for granting permission. The first: the reason must concern one of their affairs or one of their pressing concerns, so one who asks permission without an excuse is not granted it. The second: he (the Messenger) must wish to grant it, so that the public interest is served without harm to the one granting it. He said: ﴿So when they ask your permission for some matter of theirs, grant permission to whom you will among them.﴾ If a man has an excuse and asks permission, then if his staying behind and not going serves a purpose, in the Messenger's judgment, such as his opinion or his courage or the like, he does not grant him permission. Nevertheless, if he asks and is granted permission under these two conditions, God commanded His Messenger to seek forgiveness for him for whatever shortcoming he may have had in asking permission. For this reason He said: ﴿And ask God's forgiveness for them. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ He forgives them their sins and shows them mercy by permitting them to ask for leave when they have an excuse.

{63} ﴿Do not make the call of the Messenger among you like the call of some of you to others.﴾ [That is, do not make your calling of the Messenger, and your calling upon him, like the calling of some of you to one another.] So when he calls you, respond to him as an obligation. Indeed, responding to the Messenger (ﷺ) is obligatory even during prayer. No one, when he speaks, is to be accepted and acted upon by the community as obligatory except the Messenger, because of his infallibility and because we are commanded to follow him. God the Exalted said: ﴿O you who have believed, respond to God and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life.﴾ Likewise, do not make your calling of the Messenger like the calling of some of you to others. So do not say, "O Muhammad!" when you call him, or "O Muhammad, son of Abdullah!" as some of you say to one another. Rather, out of his honor, virtue, and distinction (ﷺ) above others, it should be said: "O Messenger of God! O Prophet of God!" ﴿God already knows those among you who slip away, concealing themselves.﴾ When He praised the believers in God and His Messenger, who, when they were with him on a matter requiring gathering, did not leave until they asked his permission, He threatened those who did not do this and left without asking permission. Even if their departure is hidden from you in a concealed manner, which is what is meant by His words ﴿slipping away from among you under cover﴾, that is, they hide themselves at the moment of slipping away and departing behind something that screens them from the eyes, God knows them, and He will repay them for that in the fullest measure. For this reason He threatened them by saying: ﴿So let those who oppose his order beware.﴾ That is, they go off to some of their affairs against the order of God and His Messenger. How much more so, then, is the one who did not go off to any affair of his own but simply abandoned God's command without any preoccupation. ﴿Lest a trial strike them﴾, that is, shirk and evil, ﴿or a painful punishment strike them.﴾

{64} ﴿Unquestionably, to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth.﴾ Ownership and servants, whom He disposes of by His divine decree (qadari) and His legislative command (shar'i). ﴿He already knows your condition.﴾ That is, His knowledge encompasses what you are upon of good and evil, and He knows all your deeds. His knowledge has counted them, His pen has recorded them, and the noble recording angels have written them down for you. ﴿And the Day they are returned to Him﴾, that is, the Day of Resurrection, ﴿He will inform them of what they did﴾, informing them of all their deeds, the minute and the great, with an account that corresponds exactly to what occurred from them, and He will call their own limbs as witnesses against them, so they will not lack from Him either favor or justice. Having restricted His knowledge to their deeds, He then mentioned the general after the specific, saying: ﴿And God is Knowing of all things.﴾
